note: Forest Service campground in a bend of the West Fork of the Black River north-west of Centerville: paved spurs on a wooded bottom, the outer sites backing onto the timbered river bank with a gravel-bar beach below. It serves the Sutton Bluff ATV and motorcycle trail system, so machines ride through to the trailhead (road surfaces only) and it is busy on riding weekends. Sites 29, 32 and 33 have short spurs. In the old lead-mining district; the Forest Service capped affected campsites with clean fill in 2015 and rates the exposure risk low. The last 3 miles are on County Road 849. --Claude
summary: Forest Service page and rec.gov both read and agree: $10 non-electric / $20 electric, 14 electric sites at 50 A with no water or sewer hookups, flush/vault toilets, showers, drinking water. Site count is 32 plus a group site, not the stored 61. Season about late March to end of October (closed now). Weekend 2-night minimum, 8 first-come sites. A general campground that serves an OHV trail system, not a staging lot - stays, with the caveat in the note. Riverfront is thin: lead downward flagged. policy_ref should be federal:usfs.
flags: SITE COUNT: stored 61 (the note's '24 electric + 37 non-electric') is wrong. rec.gov's catalog has 32 individual sites - 14 electric (004, 006, 023-034) and 18 non-electric - plus group site 015 and a day-use pavilion. The Forest Service page says 'Electric: 14, Nonelectric: 19, Group: Nonelectric: 1'. Written 32 from the per-site catalog; the one-site difference with the FS non-electric figure is not resolved.

OHV (criteria check - STAYS, caveat proposed): the Forest Service page says 'This campground serves the nearby Sutton Bluff ATV and Motorcycle Trail System' and 'ATV use in the campground limited to ingress and egress to the trail; must stay on road surfaces'. It is a built loop campground with paved spurs, showers and a river beach that the agency describes first as a river campground; trail parking for 10 trailers is a separate lot. That is a general campground with an OHV side, not a staging camp. Caveat written into the note.

WATERFRONT LEAD (stored riverfront; evidence points DOWN): counted on the 0.42 m/px leaf-off frame with site coordinates plotted. The campground fills a river bend, but a belt of bank timber runs between every outer site and the water. Nearest: 014 about 27 m and 013 about 35 m from the channel, through roughly 25 m of trees; 011, 009, 007, 005, 003, 002 on the west side are 55-90 m from the gravel bar and farther from the water; 016-019 on the south-east are 50-70 m back in timber. No site sits on an open apron; none has an open view in leaf. So 2 of 32 sites are within 50 m, both under canopy. rec.gov tags 18 sites 'Riverfront' (a type-level tag, not evidence) and the FS page says 'a number of campsites sit alongside the West Fork'. Canopy means imagery cannot confirm; under the rule that unsure goes down, riverview is the supportable value, or riverfront only on the strength of 013/014. Owner's call; not changed here.

SEASON: the FS page gives 2026 as April 2 to November 1; rec.gov's rate season was 2026-04-02 to 10-26 and is 03-27 to 10-30 for 2027 and 2028, and the calendar opens on 2027-03-27. Written from rec.gov's upcoming season with the 2026 dates in the season note. Closed now.

LEAD ALERT: the FS page carries the standing forest-wide alert 'Reducing Lead Exposure Risk at Campgrounds' (soil lead from the old mining district; contaminated areas capped at 100 campsites and day-use areas in 2015; 'The risks of lead exposure at these sites are generally considered to be low'). The alert does not list which sites; its presence on this page is what ties it here. One clause in the note - owner may prefer to cut it.

RIG FIT: paved spurs, 'up to 50 ft' on most sites; shortest catalog length is 40 ft. Access is county gravel/paved (CR 907 for 7 miles, CR 849 for 3); 'Vehicle Clearance - No restrictions'. No 4WD wording.
